 The transition to permanent daylight saving time in Manitoba has sparked debate, as many face challenges with later sunrises in winter and adjusting schedules. The author proposes considering a provincial vote to decide whether to keep daylight time year-round, revert to standard time, or return to biannual clock changes.

 A new Angus Reid poll found 59% of Manitoba respondents thought ending the time changes was the right move. But 64% said they’d already run into a problem or annoyance since we skipped the fall change.
 Photo credit Klein Media 
 M y biggest beef with Manitoba staying on daylight saving time is the later start for Saturday Night Live. I know it’s the weekend, but 11:30 is getting a bit late for this guy.
 I’m no fan of the dark mornings, either. Parents are certainly grumbling about it, with some of them sending their kids to school in high-vis gear. By late December, the sun won’t come up in Winnipeg until almost 9:30. Come summer, though, those long, bright evenings might make this whole thing a lot easier to live with.

 I thought based on survey results we have seen the majority was in favor of maintaining day light saving time year round, personally I'm fine with either, just as long as the twice a year abomination is gone. So leave it alone now, the change has been made and we'll all get used to it, since really, it doesn't matter which solution is the one adopted, there will always be some that complain about what has been implemented.
